title: Adaptive latency budgets and capacity tokens for region routing
creator: Maya Singh
description:
Goal: Implement an adaptive multi-region routing policy that enforces per-tenant latency budgets, uses capacity tokens to avoid overcommitting hotspots, and performs staged circuit-breaking + load-shedding before global failover. This ticket defines the policy, data signals, implementation plan, and rollout strategy.

Motivation: Current geo-steering falls back bluntly to other regions when a single region saturates, causing sudden cost spikes, cross-region tail latency, and user-visible errors. We need a smoother degradation path that keeps most traffic local when possible, preserves SLOs, and provides predictable operational controls.

Key ideas:
- Latency budget per region: maintain a short EWMA-based latency estimate per model/region and compute a per-tenant latency budget (target percentile + slack). Traffic steering prefers regions whose EWMA + safety margin is within budget.
- Capacity token buckets: each region exposes a token pool per tenant (or per-route) representing headroom based on queue length, GPU utilization, and recent rejection rate. Tokens are issued by the regional admission controller and consumed on request dispatch; token exhaustion prevents additional hedging to that region.
- Staged circuit-breaker: multiple thresholds with different actions:
  * threshold-1 (soft): when 80% tokens used OR p95 > budget -> start minor shedding (5-10%) and reduce hedging to region.
  * threshold-2 (hard): when 95% tokens used OR sustained > budget for 30s -> halt new routed requests (fast fail to fallback) and increase shedding (20-50%).
  * threshold-3 (drain): when sustained > budget for 2m OR queue growth accelerating -> enable local degrade (lower-quality model variant or quantized profile) and trigger ops page.
- Graceful pin eviction: implement a probabilistic pin eviction curve where locality pinning decays when region tokens deplete, instead of immediate unpin. This reduces client churn and gives prefetched caches KV time to be useful.
- Model-variant fallback: routing supports downgrade path to compatible lighter-weight model variants (e.g., int8/quantized or smaller architecture) when region capacity is low; fallback decisions are cost-aware and subject to quality guards.
- Observability & controls: surface token counts, EWMA latencies, circuit state, and shed rate in Console per-route dashboard; expose per-tenant overrides and an emergency global-shed switch.

Design trade-offs and considerations:
- Token latency vs correctness: tokens are small (~4-16B) and can be stale. We use short TTL (1s) and conservative replenishment to avoid oscillation.
- State explosion: tokens per-tenant could be many. We'll aggregate by billing-customer when possible and only enable per-route tokens for flagged high-risk tenants.
- Quality regressions: variant fallback must be gated by evaluation harness or do AB compare on a sample of traffic.
- Safety: no automated hard failover without manual or rule-based escalation for enterprise customers unless SLOs are critically violated.

Implementation sketch:
1) Admission controller change (regional): expose an API /tokens/{tenant}/{route} returning available tokens, issued tokens, and estimated replenishment rate. Integrate with existing regional scaler metrics (GPU queue length, utilization, pending requests).
2) Global routing layer: add a token-aware allocator. Request flow: check locality pin -> request tokens from preferred region -> if tokens >= 1 and EWMA < budget -> dispatch; else consult fallback list (other regions, model-variants) and apply shedding policy.
3) Circuit breaker state machine: maintain per-(region,tenant,route) three-state counters and cooldown windows.
4) Pin eviction algorithm: probabilistic decay with hysteresis.
5) Metrics & logs: token_requests, tokens_granted, token_exhaustions, shed_rate, p50/p95/p99 per region/route, model-fallback-events, circuit_state_changes.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 0 (lab): simulated traffic replay using past 30 days of production traces to verify stability and oscillation behavior.
- Phase 1 (canary): enable for internal staging tenants and 5 low-risk customers, monitoring Console dashboards and error budgets for 72h.
- Phase 2 (targeted opt-in): enable for mid-tier customers with opt-in flag; collect quality/latency regressions.
- Phase 3 (gradual default): turn on for all non-enterprise tenants with conservative thresholds; enterprise customers get a managed rollout that requires approval.

Runbook (ops):
- If region token_exhaustions spike: 1) increase token replenishment temporarily, 2) reduce quantization fallback aggressiveness, 3) if still failing, manually enable cross-region hedging for affected tenants.
- If oscillation observed (traffic bouncing between regions): 1) increase EWMA window and backoff on pin evictions, 2) engage engineering to tune thresholds.

Deliverables: design doc (link below), admission-controller PR, router changes, circuit-breaker library, console dashboard tiles, e2e tests and replay harness, rollout checklist.
acceptance_criteria: Router can consult region token API and make dispatch decisions based on token availability
Three-stage circuit-breaker implemented with configurable thresholds and cooldowns
EWMA-based latency budget computed per region and used in steering decision loop
Probabilistic pin eviction implemented and shown to reduce cross-region churn in replay tests
Model-variant fallback executed for >1000 requests in staging with no >1% quality regression on sampled evals
Console shows token metrics, circuit states, and shed rates per-route and per-tenant
Canary rollout completes for internal tenants without SLO violations over 72h
